title: Results Ledger
read_first: None of these results has been peer reviewed. They are preprints by one independent author, produced with disclosed AI assistance.
"Lean kernel" means the Lean 4 kernel accepted the proof. That certifies the formal statement, not the choice of statement, so every result also records a statement audit.

The audit recorded for each result was run by AI review agents in sessions separate from the ones that wrote the proofs, under the author's direction: a clean rebuild at the cited commit, a reading of the formal statement against the claim and its cited source, and a literature search. It is an internal check, not external review.
A result answers only the question stated. Parent problems named in the papers remain open unless they are listed here.
not_claimed: No Millennium Prize problem and no grand open problem is solved here. P versus NP is open.
No result has been refereed by a journal or checked by a named outside expert.
Engineering invariant suites (section F) verify software models. They are not evidence about consciousness, sentience, biology or physics.
A search that found no earlier proof is not a proof of novelty.
admission_rules: The claim is registered in the archive with a pinned commit and a frozen paper.
The formal statement is read against the informal claim and against the cited source, in a session that did not write the proof.
The proof is rebuilt from a clean clone at that commit, or the ledger says it was not.
The literature is searched for earlier or parallel proofs and the outcome is recorded.
The wording is limited to what steps 2 to 4 support. Anything narrower than the usual informal claim is stated under Limit.
challenge: Open an issue on this repository or on the result's repository and quote the result number (for example R7).
A reproducible counterexample, a gap in a statement audit, or an earlier proof in the literature leads to a correction: the result is narrowed, reclassified or withdrawn, and keeps its number.

entries_without_results.0TH-2026-001: Archived v1.0.0 snapshot whose third-moment bound and corollaries were consolidated into 0TH-2026-009; recording them here too would count the same results twice.
entries_without_results.0TH-BUILD-006: No machine-checked result at the pinned commit. Its Lean file (eight literal arithmetic identities) is on an unmerged branch; the build itself is a C++ ray-tracing lab.

results.title: Digit-sum characterisation of two-register passive register programs with F_p constants
results.statement: For p prime, t ≥ 1, f ∈ F_p[x]: a passive two-register program (instructions O += P(R), R += c, O += λx, R += λx; constants in F_p) with at most t input accesses producing O + f(x) and restoring R, as an identity of formal polynomials in F_p[R, x], exists exactly when every d ≥ 2 with [x^d]f ≠ 0 has base-p digit sum s_p(d) ≤ min(p−1, t−1).
results.evidence_note: Formal identity implies correct execution in every commutative ring of characteristic p (proved, T1s); the converse step is a paper argument.
limits: Cleanliness means equality of formal polynomials; as functions on F_p itself x^p = x, so for example x^3 over F_2 is computed with one input access although the theorem excludes it.
Program constants lie in the prime field; with F_4 constants the criterion changes (x^3 becomes computable), and the case of general F_(p^e) is open.

Vinciguerra (arXiv:2609.18692) proves the characteristic-0 analogue (Theorem 3.5) and does not pose the positive-characteristic question; this is a self-posed extension, not an answer to a published question.
Two registers only; nothing is shown for three or more registers in positive characteristic.
That literal clean execution over a polynomial ring implies the formal predicate (needed to read the 'only if' half as a statement about executions) is not formalised.
Prior-work search was limited to arXiv, Semantic Scholar and one web query on 2026-11-26.

results.title: Two-access programs for x^(2^k) in characteristic 2 using product updates only
results.statement: For k ≥ 1 and every commutative ring with 2 = 0, a program on k+1 registers with instructions R_d += R_a·R_b (d ∉ {a, b}; register 0 never read) and R_d += x uses 2 input accesses and 4k−2 products, adds x^(2^k) to register 0 and restores the others, from every initial state. With k+2 registers and copies R_d += R_s, the indices d, a, b are pairwise distinct.
results.evidence_note: Elementary: repeated squaring with (a+b)² = a² + b² in characteristic 2.
limits: Characteristic 2 only.
No lower bound on registers, products or input accesses is proved.
The product-only instruction set is the repository's restriction of the register-program model; the statement is not tied to a published question.
Only general searches of the register-program literature were run; the underlying identity is standard.
results.check: cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean

results.title: Four-register passive powering of x^N with fewer than (104/3)·N^(log₁₃ 8) input accesses
results.statement: Let N ≥ 1 have ℓ+1 base-13 digits. Over every commutative ring in which D_8 = 2656207148788801777680, 12! and (ℓ+1)! are invertible, some passive four-register program maps (o, u, r₁, r₂) to (o + x^N, u, r₁, r₂) with fewer than (104/3)·8^ℓ ≤ (104/3)·N^(log₁₃ 8) input accesses. Counting ℓ+1 base-7 digits instead: 6! and (ℓ+1)! invertible, fewer than (70/3)·5^ℓ accesses. The base-13 bound is also stated coordinatewise over Rⁿ.
results.evidence_note: Lean states 3·accesses < 104·8^ℓ with 13^ℓ ≤ N; the real-exponent form and the comparison with log₅ 4 are paper-level conversions.
limits: Improves the exponent of Corollary 4.3.1 of arXiv:2609.18692 at four registers (log₅ 4 ≈ 0.8614 to log₁₃ 8 ≈ 0.8107); with the stated constants the bound is smaller than 20·N^(log₅ 4) only for N above about 52,000 (base-7 variant: above about 90).

No lower bound is proved: log₁₃ 8 is the smallest exponent among the constructed base programs (t = 8 minimises log_(2t−3) t over integers t ≥ 4, which is integer arithmetic), not a proven optimum for three-register base programs.
In prime characteristic p the hypotheses exclude p ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 137, 1602207194491} and require p > ℓ+1, which limits N.
With five registers the cited paper already has the smaller exponent log₇ 4 ≈ 0.712.
The coordinatewise corollary contains no stream model or space bound; the streaming and matrix-powering applications are paper arguments outside Lean.

results.title: Lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of the odd cycles C₂₅ and C₂₉
results.statement: C₂₅^⊠144 contains an independent set of size M with 12344196091426841^144 ≤ M·10^(15·144), and C₂₉^⊠4 contains an independent set of size 42050, where 14319949949077991^4 ≤ 42050·10^60. Consequently Θ(C₂₅) ≥ 12.344196091426841 and Θ(C₂₉) ≥ 14.319949949077991. Both exceed the largest earlier values found, 23125^(1/4) ≈ 12.3316 and 42017^(1/4) ≈ 14.3171 (Codenotti–Gerace–Resta 2003, Table 1).
results.evidence_note: Θ is not defined in Lean; the capacity bounds follow from the integer statements by Θ(G) = sup α(G^⊠d)^(1/d).
limits: Lower bounds only; the exact value of Θ(C_n) is open for every odd n ≥ 7.
The margins over the 2003 values are 0.01257 (C₂₅) and 0.00281 (C₂₉, 33 more words in the fourth power), smaller than the gains the repository states against third-power values.
The C₂₅ base set has the 2003 published size 23125; the gain comes from a port system and the Buys–Polak–Zuiddam substitution tables, whose framework this follows.
The prior-work search was not exhaustive: Baumert et al. 1971 and Hales 1973 were not opened, and the 2003 table entries are printed cardinalities.

results.title: Independent sets in the fourth strong power of C_n for n = 4m+1
results.statement: For every m ≥ 5 with m ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4) and n = 4m+1: α(C_n^⊠4) ≥ (m² + ⌊m/4⌋)·n². The set is lifted from m² + ⌊m/4⌋ = ⌊n⌊n/4⌋/4⌋ points of ℤ_n², no two within circular distance 3 in both coordinates; no such point set is larger (n ≥ 4), and each one of size M lifts to M·n² points (n ≥ 9).
results.evidence_note: Three contract theorems: lifting (T1a), ceiling (T1b), family (T1d).
limits: For m ≡ 0 (mod 4), n = 16j+1, the size equals (n⁴−n³)/16, the exact value of α(C_n^⊠4) credited to Baumert et al. (1971) in the 2003 paper of Codenotti, Gerace and Resta.
The case n = 21 (11466 words, 26 cosets of ⟨(1,0,0,2),(0,1,2,0)⟩) is in the 2026 Lean repository of Buys, Polak and Zuiddam.
For m ≡ 1 (mod 4), m ≥ 9, the sizes exceed the 2003 table entries at n = 37 and n = 53 (113627 vs 113586, 483148 vs 483091); no search for later work on these n was done.
The ceiling bounds unions of cosets of one subgroup, not α(C_n^⊠4); Lean proves the lifting direction only.

results.title: Minimum Kochen-Specker set in the 49-ray integer pool B(3,2)
results.statement: Let B(3,2) be the 49 primitive rays of ℤ³ with entries in {−2,…,2}. Some 31 of them admit no Kochen–Specker colouring (no two orthogonal rays coloured 1, every orthogonal triple inside the set containing a ray coloured 1), and every subset of at most 30 of them admits one.
results.evidence_note: The pool list is proved equal to all such rays, each once (rays_eq, boxRays_exact).
limits: Only rays inside B(3,2) are considered; the unrestricted minimum in dimension three (QM-011) is not affected.
The value 31 was reported earlier by Kernaghan (arXiv:2603.16988, v1–v9), whose v10 calls that earlier certification unsound.
An independent Lean proof for the same pool appeared in arXiv:2603.16988v10 on 23 Nov 2026, after this repository's v1.0.0 of 10 Nov 2026.
That there are exactly six minimum sets is not part of the Lean theorem.

results.title: Input-access counts for x^3, x^5 and x^7 in two-register passive programs over F_4
results.statement: For passive two-register programs with constants in the field F_4 and equality of formal polynomials in F_4[R, x]: x^5 is produced with 3 input accesses and not with 2; x^3 is produced with 4 input accesses and not with 3; x^7 is produced with no number of input accesses.
results.evidence_note: F_4 is an explicit four-element type with table-defined operations and a proved commutative-ring instance.
limits: Three monomials over one field; no general criterion for F_(p^e) is proved.
Formal-polynomial cleanliness as in T1; as functions on F_4, x^7 = x.
Not posed in the cited literature.

results.title: Three-register passive programs for x^(2t−3) with t = 5, …, 9 input accesses
results.statement: For t = 5,…,9 and every commutative ring in which the integer D_t is invertible, a passive program on registers (O, u, v) with exactly t input accesses maps (o, u, v) to (o + x^(2t−3), u, v) for all x, o, u, v. D_5 = 576, D_6 = 382500000; D_7, D_8, D_9 have 23, 22 and 51 digits. Hence D^pass_3(t) ≥ 2t−3 for these t over such fields.
results.evidence_note: Also re-derived in this audit by exact integer polynomial arithmetic outside Lean: each program adds D_t·x^(2t−3) and restores u, v.

results.title: Frozen bit strings of the 0110↔1001 dipole-conserving gate
results.statement: Swapping 0110 and 1001 preserves charge and dipole moment. The sequence Z with Z(0..3) = 1, 2, 4, 8 and Z(L) = Z(L−1) + Z(L−2) + Z(L−4) equals the number of length-L bit strings avoiding 0110 and 1001 for L = 1, …, 6, and satisfies 2Z(L) < Z(L+4) for L ≥ 1. Over ℤ, x⁴ − x³ − x² − 1 = (x+1)(x³ − 2x² + x − 1).
results.evidence_note: Count identity kernel-checked for L ≤ 6 only; agreement for larger L is computational (L ≤ 14 in the repository, L ≤ 15 in this audit).
limits: The 'Plastic-constant-squared' conjunct is vacuous: ρ³ = ρ + 1 has no integer solution.
The growth rate ρ² and Θ(ρ^(2L)) are not in Lean.
'Skin-effect immunity' of frozen strings follows directly from the definition of frozen.
The counting sequence coincides with OEIS A164394 (stated there for the pattern pair 0001, 0100) on L = 0..15; exponentially many frozen states are known (Sala et al. 2020; Khemani et al. 2020).

results.title: Algebraic closed forms of the Banić–Elezović recombination expressions for γ(n), γ_c(n), γ(3;N), γ(4;N)
results.statement: With p₁ = (n²−4n−4)/(32πn), q₁ = a_△·n/π − (n+1)/(8πn), r₁ = −(n+1)/(8πn) and a_△ = 1/32 − 4√3/243: for real n ≠ 0, (n−1)p₁ + 2(n−2)q₁ + (n−2)(n−3)r₁ = −n(n+1)/(32π) − 8√3·n(n−2)/(243π) + (n−1)/(8πn), and n·p₁ + 2n·q₁ + n(n−3)r₁ = −n(n+4)/(32π) − 8√3·n²/(243π). Two analogous identities hold at n = 3 and n = 4.
results.evidence_note: Identities between real numbers only. That the left sides are variance coefficients is taken from Banić–Elezović, outside Lean.

asked_in.citation: N. Banić, N. Elezović, Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 2: variance under the uniform null (2026), arXiv:2610.17046
asked_in.locator: Theorem 7.6 and the consequences stated after Conjecture 7.7; for γ_c, Theorem 3.10 of Part 5, arXiv:2611.14735

limits: Lean defines no random variable, variance or expansion in N. That these expressions are the N⁻² coefficients of Var(d)/N rests on Theorem 7.6, Lemmas 7.2, 7.3, 7.5 and Section 8 of arXiv:2610.17046v1 and Theorem 3.10 of arXiv:2611.14735v1, which are unrefereed and not formalized.
The closed forms are already printed in the source as consequences conditional on Conjecture 7.7; these theorems machine-check that algebra.
In Lean n is any nonzero real; the source's statements are for integer n ≥ 5, with n = 3 and n = 4 treated separately.
In the n = 4 identity the term (−1)^N/(2π) appears unchanged on both sides, so the dependence on N is carried, not derived.

results.title: Inequalities for the Hill function of order four in cleared-denominator form
results.statement: For natural numbers c, c1 < c2 and kd > 0, with x⁴ written out: c⁴ < c⁴ + kd⁴; c⁴/(c⁴+kd⁴) is strictly increasing in c; it is at most 1/82 when 3c ≤ kd; the ratio of its values at kd and kd/2 is 17/2; it lies below c/(c+kd) when c < kd and above when c > kd; and 2·kd⁴ = kd⁴ + kd⁴.
results.axioms: propext, Quot.sound (T03: none; T06: propext only)
limits: Statements are over natural numbers with denominators cleared; no real-valued Hill function or Ca²⁺ model is defined.
T02 is the identity 2x = x + x and its hypothesis kd > 0 is unused.
These are textbook properties; a prior public Lean 4 formalisation of Hill monotonicity exists (marpaia/grn-lean, per the literature audit).

results.title: Integer bounds for a short-term-plasticity step, conductance means, a blocking factor and 2×2 determinants
results.statement: Over integers with stated positivity, denominators cleared: one Tsodyks–Markram step u⁺ = u + ⌊u₀(S−u)/S⌋ keeps u ≤ u⁺ ≤ S and releases at most x; eI·G ≤ Σgᵢeᵢ ≤ eE·G, strictly lowered when gI > 0; D/(D+m·e) < 1, decreasing in e; σ²N < σ²NK for K ≥ 2; kc/(kc+kOff) increases in c; rank-one 2×2 tables have det 0; diagonal excess gives |det| > 0.
results.axioms: propext, Quot.sound (T21: none; T23: propext only)

T10 states two numerator identities; the divisive ratio (gL+gE)/(gL+gE+gI) is not itself a Lean statement.
T07 covers one spike update only, and its hypothesis u₀ > 0 is unused.
T22–T24 concern four integers and contain no notion of integration, causality or nanocolumn structure; they are also listed under companion entry 0TH-2026-008.

results.title: Clean product of 2^k inputs by a balanced four-step telescoping recursion
results.statement: For every k, sign ±1 and duplicate-free register list target :: pool with |pool| ≥ k+1 when k ≥ 1, a program of (7·4^k − 4)/3 instructions of the forms R_i ± x_l and R_i ± R_a·R_b (i, a, b pairwise distinct) adds ± x_off · … · x_(off+2^k−1) to the target register and leaves every other register unchanged, over every commutative ring and from every initial state.
results.evidence_note: Variant of the classical four-term clean-product recursion; the exact instruction count in this instruction set was not located in the literature.
limits: The publicly quoted register count log₂ d + 2 is not a conjunct of the Lean statement at the audited commit; it is read off the program definition (the conjunct was added upstream after this commit).

Overlap with earlier work: Ben-Or and Cleve (SIAM J. Comput. 1992) give polynomial-length three-register programs for all polynomial-size formulas in a neighbouring instruction set and report earlier logarithmic-register methods; the paper does not position this result against them.
No lower bound is proved; the words 'optimal' and 'sharp' used for this result in the paper are unsupported.
Number of inputs is a power of two.

results.title: ML-KEM parameter arithmetic and a Compress_1 decoding margin
results.statement: 3329 is prime and 17 has multiplicative order 256 modulo 3329; signed Montgomery reduction returns r with r·2^16 ≡ a (mod 3329) and |r| < 3329 for |a| < 2^15·3329; for b ∈ {0,1} and |e| ≤ 831 the repository's Lean function mlkemCompress1 maps b·1665 + e to b.
results.evidence_note: mlkemCompress1 uses offset 1665 and differs from FIPS 203 Compress_1 only at x = 832, which this margin statement never reaches.
limits: The Lean Compress_1 model is not FIPS 203: it returns 1 at x = 832 where FIPS 203 returns 0.
The companion claim that both b = 0 and b = 1 fail at e = +832 (adv_compress1_fails_at_plus_832, the CI negative test, the paper) is false for FIPS 203; only b = 1 fails.
No statement about ML-KEM security or full decryption correctness is formalized.
The margin condition is the standard Kyber/ML-KEM correctness condition and has earlier machine-checked treatments.
results.check: cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean

results.title: Combinatorial cores of one-time pad, XOR combining, Toeplitz hashing, Shamir sharing and Reed–Solomon decoding
results.statement: Over Boolean vectors: the one-time-pad key and each XOR-combiner factor are unique given the rest; a Toeplitz pivot window is uniquely determined. Over any SimpleField: a nonzero polynomial with at most d+1 coefficients has at most d distinct roots; t points determine f(0) for length ≤ t; t−1 shares are consistent with every secret; f(0) is uniquely decodable when n ≥ t + 2b.
limits: Probabilistic secrecy, universal-hash collision probability and the leftover hash lemma are not formalized; only bijection and counting cores are.
The 'tightness' part of t3b is only the arithmetic d = 2b; no counterexample is built.
All are textbook results (Shannon 1949, Carter–Wegman, Shamir 1979, Reed–Solomon decoding).
results.check: cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean

results.title: Total-variation/overlap identity and classical Fuchs–van de Graaf bounds for finite distributions
results.statement: For P0, P1 : ℕ → ℕ with equal totals D: Σ|P0−P1| + 2·Σmin(P0,P1) = 2D, with three corollaries. For r, s : ℕ → ℕ with Σr² = Σs² = M and B = Σ r·s: overlap ≤ B ≤ M, 2M ≤ TV₂ + 2B and TV₂² + 4B² ≤ 4M²; and |⟨u,v⟩|² ≤ M² for complex integer vectors of squared norm M.
limits: No commitment protocol is formalized; bit-commitment impossibility and 'architectural necessity' are informal readings.
Only the classical case with perfect-square integer weights is covered; quantum Fuchs–van de Graaf for density operators is not.
The pure-state relation D_tr² + F = 1 holds by the definition of D_tr² in Lean.
No EFI pair or computational indistinguishability is defined.

results.title: Polynomial identities for a one-parameter two-qubit family
results.statement: For integers with ca² + sa² = R²: (sa²−ca²)² + (2·ca·sa)² = R⁴ (read on paper as c_eff² + C² = 1); with also ch² + sh² = R², a scaled identity the paper reads as det(g) − Ω²/4 = (C²/4)·sin²(θ/2); and Cauchy–Schwarz-type bounds for sums over Gaussian-integer vectors.
results.evidence_note: Interpretation as Berry flux, concurrence, quantum geometric tensor and min-entropy is paper-level and numerical.
limits: c_eff² + C² = 1 coincides with the complementarity relation C² + S_k² = 1 of Jakob and Bergou (arXiv:quant-ph/0302075, Eq. 11), which is not cited.
No Berry curvature, Chern number, entropy or quantum geometric tensor is defined in Lean; c_eff = −cos 2α is continuous, so 'topological' and 'quantized' do not apply.

results.title: Markov's negation bound for the inverter and a k-NOT compilation
results.statement: No circuit over constants, AND, OR and NOT with at most r NOT gates computes all n negations when n ≥ 2^r. An explicit circuit with exactly k NOT gates computes all negations of 2^k − 1 inputs. Every such circuit on exactly 2^k − 1 inputs has an equivalent circuit with exactly k NOT gates; no bound on its size is proved.
limits: Fischer's 1975 theorem is a polynomial-size construction; the Lean compilation has no size bound and its inverter is exponential-size.
The upper bound and compilation cover n = 2^k − 1 only, not all n ≤ 2^k − 1.
